text: Merleau-Ponty accepts much of Husserl's phenomenology but corrects his account of time-consciousness. What is the core of his correction?
choices: Temporal experience should be analyzed as the work of a transcendental consciousness performing acts of retention and protention
The felt passage of time is an illusion generated by the memory-anticipation asymmetry of the cognitive system
The just-past is held in awareness as a still-perceived tone that has acquired an attached quality of 'pastness'
Temporal experience is grounded not in pure consciousness but in the lived, motor body, whose habits carry the past as practical disposition
explanation: Merleau-Ponty argues that consciousness is embodied and that the body itself is a temporal organization: habit (e.g., the pianist's fingers that 'know' the étude) carries the sedimented past as practical disposition rather than as mental representation. Choice 1 is precisely the Husserlian transcendental-consciousness account he judges one-sided; choice 2 is the no-passage cognitive-illusion view of Callender and Prosser; choice 3 is Brentano's modification theory. None of these is Merleau-Ponty's position.
